rv.q: In a time of polarisation and performative outrage, this show is a hymn to tolerance and the ability to laugh with others and at oneself.
This fusillade of laser-focused facetiousness feels like the perfect piffle for our turbulent times.
Ditto Patrick Marber's blissfully silly show — but this one should run and run.
The show’s many deliberate cultural tropes and stereotypes are exaggerated to the nth-degree.
It’s still a winningly funny proposition for a new generation – and Marber pulls out all the stops to raise the Garrick roof.
But you’d have to be made of stone not to laugh at it, even if the laughter is a tad rueful these days.
Outrageous, audacious and utterly unmissable, this West End revival is a triumph of impeccable casting, razor-sharp direction and a laugh-a-minute script.
The Producers has come back to the West End just at the right time, offering a giant slab of feel-good escapism and genuine hilarity when such things feel in short supply.
Only a true misery guts could pick faults in Patrick Mar
Resistance is futile when the comedy value is as relentless and impressive as it is in this delightful production.
The Producers is so totally tasteless but so funny.
Just as importantly, it’s a rattling good night out in these troubled times.

As directed by Patrick Marber, the party scene where our devious pair attempt to cajole a pseud-director Roger Debris (Trevor Ashley) and his largely pointless camp side-kick, is particularly lacking in sophistication and resorts too often to slap-stick and lewd kitsch.
It's quite a combination, but Patrick Marber's production is a sparkling, comedic masterpiece.
Whatever it is that was missing has certainly been found this time around, as the West End transfer is an obvious five-star show.
This plucky, inventive new production certainly deserves to end up on Broadway.

The fact that I physically squirmed at certain scenes, especially considering recent events in America, and then questioned my response – all while having an absolute blast – is pure testament to what an inspired show this is.

cn.t: Critics rave about this riotous West End revival, praising its daring humor and expert comic timing. Patrick Marber's production delivers non-stop belly laughs while skewering fascism and showbiz with timeless wit and vigorous sparkle.
